transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Ortega (Zenith Head DS), Samir (Zenith MLOps), Jo (Zenith CTO), Alex (Zenith PM)

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we have about 50 minutes. i'm maya, account exec at redwood.
[00:00:10] Dr. Lina: hey, lina here. i'll be leading the evaluation from data science and clinical QA side.
[00:00:14] Samir: samir, ops, i'll own infra and pilot run.
[00:00:18] Jo: jo, cto, watching for risk and compliance.
[00:00:22] Alex: alex, product, focused on user flows and latency.
[00:00:26] Ethan: ethan, se, i'll cover benchmarks and cost knobs.
[00:00:30] Maya: great. agenda is: 1) current stack & constraints, 2) success criteria, 3) sizing & cost model, 4) benchmark plan and timeline, 5) next steps.

[00:01:05] Alex: quick context — we run a triage assistant inside our provider portal. traffic pattern: big spike 9–11am PT, but otherwise low qps. average request is a short generation for summarization + follow-up suggestions, sequence length typically 150–300 tokens. we need interactive feel; goal p95 under 250ms but ideally 150–200ms.

[00:01:45] Samir: current infra is a mix — we use GCP, kubernetes, models hosted on a managed endpoint from vendor X, but costs have spiked. we're looking at either hosted Redwood or a small dedicated pool in our VPC. data residency and audit logs are musts.

[00:02:20] Maya: understood. when you say costs spiked, rough numbers? token volumes?

[00:02:28] Dr. Lina: rough — about 6 million tokens/week across production and staging. peak QPS ~220, sustained off-peak ~20. budget for pilot is tight — directionally under $8k/mo for evaluation, but willing to expand if unit economics work.

[00:03:00] Ethan: ok that's helpful. so for cost modeling we look at three levers: per-token model pricing (baseline), runtime efficiency from batching, and reuse savings from prefix/KV caching. plus infra cost (dedicated GPU hours).

[00:03:22] Jo: curious about quantization; we heard 4-bit quant can halve cost but might affect quality — what are realistic gains?

[00:03:30] Ethan: yes, with modern open models quant to 4-bit often gives ~1.6–2x improvement in throughput/cost for generation while keeping quality high for summarization. specifics depend on model family. also kernel selection and fp16 vs int8 path matter on A100/H100.

[00:04:00] [00:04:00] Dr. Lina: can you give us per-token ballpark numbers to compare to our current vendor?

[00:04:06] Maya: sure — for hosted Redwood using a mid-sized open LLM variant we typically show an all-in per-token unit cost of $0.00045–$0.0009 per output token depending on batching and quantization. with dedicated and aggressive quantization that drops toward $0.00025–$0.0004 per token. note these are illustrative.

[00:04:40] Samir: that range helps. currently vendor X charges us approx $0.00085/output token plus request overhead, but we don't get caching. how does caching change the math?

[00:04:55] Ethan: caching can reduce effective tokens by reusing prefix context. for our triage flows most prompts have a stable template + variable patient text. prefix caching can save ~15–35% of compute tokens depending on reuse. plus we have KV cache to avoid repeating KV recomputation for streaming sessions which can reduce generator work on long conversations.

[00:05:20] Alex: practical example?

[00:05:23] Ethan: say average request 250 tokens out, 50 tokens in. with a 25% prefix reuse we only compute 187.5 equivalent tokens per request. multiply by per-token cost gets you real savings. batching adds another multiplier: if we can batch 4–8 requests per micro-batch, token cost amortizes over kernel launch overhead — practical elbow usually around batch sizes 2–6 for latency-sensitive apps.

[00:06:00] [00:06:00] Jo: what about latency tradeoffs — batching hurts tail latency, right?

[00:06:05] Ethan: correct — batching increases queuing. our continuous batching engine targets sub-20ms micro-batch windows for interactive flows, so p95 hit depends on load and chosen policy. for your target p95 200ms, we can usually batch lightly (batch size 2–3) and keep p95 within goal while still gaining 10–25% per-token cost improvement.

[00:06:40] Dr. Lina: nice. what about benchmark plan — how long should we run and what metrics will you collect?

[00:06:46] Ethan: we recommend a two-phase benchmark: 1) synthetic throughput run (48 hours) simulating your 9–11am spike pattern and median seq length 256; 2) replay of sampled production traces for quality and p95 validation (1 week if you can share traces, otherwise 2 days for smaller sample). collect metrics: request qps, p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, effective token cost, memory/KV hit rates, and failure/error rates.

[00:07:20] Samir: we can share sanitized traces for replay. storage of logs — do you provide audit logs in private deployments?

[00:07:26] Maya: yes, Redwood Private includes audit logs and optional S3 audit export. Hosted can provide consolidated logs with masking; for regulated PHI data you'd likely want Private with our customer-managed VPC or bring-your-own-key for KMS.

[00:07:50] Alex: timeline — we're hoping to have a pilot in 3 weeks, with a decision within 6 weeks. realistic?

[00:07:57] Maya: yes, realistic. proposed timeline: this week share pricing + config, week 2 run synthetic hosted benchmark (48 hrs) + replay, week 3 analyze results and spin up pilot (either 1–2 dedicated GPUs in your VPC or hosted with dedicated capacity). decision meeting end of week 3.

[00:08:20] [00:08:20] Dr. Lina: success criteria — let me list: 1) p95 latency <= 200ms for typical summarization route, 2) end-to-end cost below $8k/mo for pilot traffic equivalent, 3) no material drop in model quality (ROUGE / human spot checks), 4) audit and key management acceptable.

[00:08:50] Maya: copied. we'll create a success-criteria table in the follow-up email.

[00:09:05] Samir: coach me on pilot sizing — given 6M tokens/week, and peaks, what suggested pilot capacity?

[00:09:12] Ethan: quick back-of-envelope: 6M tokens/week is ~857k tokens/day, about 1.0–1.5M tokens on peak days depending on distribution. If average output tokens per request is 200, that's ~4–7k requests/day, but peak QPS matters: you mentioned 220 qps. For interactive p95 200ms you'd want either a hosted config with autoscaling to sustain peaks or 1–2 A100/H100-like GPUs in dedicated mode with batching and caching tuned.

[00:09:50] Ethan: numeric example: hosted per-output-token $0.0006 baseline -> 6M tokens/week => ~ $3,600/week, oops wipe math wait — let me recalc, 6M tokens/week * $0.0006 = $3,600, yes that maps to $14,400/mo, which is above your target. but with caching (25% savings) and quantization to 4-bit (~1.8x improvement), you could get effective cost down to about $5k–$7k/mo. Dedicated reserved capacity often reduces the per-token unit further if you commit.

[00:10:30] Jo: those math variations are critical. can you outline assumptions for that calc so we can run sensitivity?

[00:10:36] Ethan: assumptions: baseline per-output-token price $0.0006 (hosted, fp16), average tokens/out 200, avg reuse 25% from caching, quantization factor 1.8x improvement, batching efficiency 1.15x. Combined effective multiplier = 0.75 (caching) / 1.8 (quant) / 1.15 (batch) approximate -> effective per-token ~ $0.0006 * 0.36 = $0.000216. Multiply 6M/week => $1,296/week -> ~$5,184/mo. if any assumption moves (less reuse, lower quant quality) numbers change.

[00:11:15] Dr. Lina: good to see the algebra. we will run sensitivity in our spreadsheet. can redwood share a model-specific profile (e.g., perf on A100 vs H100, batching curves)?

[00:11:24] Maya: yes, ethan will attach our perf profiles and kernel/batching curves and recommended instance types.

[00:11:35] [00:11:35] Alex: security: for pilot we need SOC2 + data deletion policy + SSO. how do these map to hosted vs private?

[00:11:43] Maya: hosted has SOC 2 Type II and SSO options; for strict deletion/deidentification and customer-controlled keys we'd recommend Redwood Private in your VPC. for pilot we can do hosted with masked logs but if you need PHI in full we push towards Private.

[00:12:05] Samir: one more infra Q — can we run a quick side-by-side: hosted Redwood variant vs dedicated in our VPC for latency and cost?

[00:12:12] Ethan: yes, our proposed benchmark will include a hosted run and a dedicated run (if you can approve temporary dedicated nodes). for dedicated we need a one-week minimum to setup and get warm caches; hosted we can spin up in hours.

[00:12:35] Dr. Lina: what's the minimum data we need to share for trace replay?

[00:12:39] Maya: sanitized request/response logs with consistent IDs, timestamp, request prompt length and output length. remove PHI. schema example we'll send.

[00:12:52] [00:12:52] Samir: on the topic of cost accounting — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns by route so we can attribute to product features?

[00:12:58] Maya: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route cost and token breakdowns, token-level attribution, and trace links to requests. that's part of the metrics we can show during the pilot.

[00:13:18] Alex: a question about failure modes — if a model falls back or we exceed capacity, how do you degrade gracefully?

[00:13:24] Ethan: we have automatic fallback policies: route to smaller model variant, or degrade to a cached summary. you can set routing policies by latency vs cost; we can also return partial responses relying on KV cache for continuity.

[00:13:40] Dr. Lina: quality validation — we want both automated metrics and human spot checks. can Redwood run evals on generated summaries?

[00:13:46] Maya: yes, we offer eval hooks and can run batch evaluations (ROUGE/BLEU and human spot checks) as part of the pilot. we'll propose an evaluation plan.

[00:14:10] [00:14:10] Ethan: ok i'm going to walk through a sample cost worksheet live — apologies if numbers are a bit rough on the fly.

[00:14:15] Ethan: baseline cost lines: model runtime $/GPU-hour, tokens per second throughput, per-token runtime cost = GPU-hour cost / tokens-served-hour. hosted overlays model licensing or infra fee. then applied multipliers for caching/batching/quant.

[00:14:42] Ethan: example numbers: H100 equivalent GPU cost to us $6.00/hr (this is our internal infra amortized number), throughput for 1 model at seq=256 and batch 1 = 450 tokens/sec, so tokens/hr ~1.62M. per-token raw infra cost $6.00 / 1.62M = $0.0000037 per token (infrastructure only). then add model infra fee & management and you get closer to the $0.0004–$0.0009 range depending on config.

[00:15:20] Alex: wow the infra-only number is tiny; the rest is licensing and ops overhead.

[00:15:24] Ethan: yep, that's why batching and caching matter — they change tokens served/hr effectively.

[00:15:40] [00:15:40] Jo: any red flags for us doing private? network egress/hot sharding complexity?

[00:15:45] Ethan: main friction points: private requires a longer setup (network, KMS, FRR), need to size GPUs for peaks (no autoscaling without extra ops), and you manage OS/pipeline updates unless you choose managed private where we do that. but you get full control over keys and logs.

[00:16:05] Dr. Lina: for the pilot decision — if we aim for $8k/mo target, can we run two variants in parallel and pick the winner?

[00:16:12] Maya: yes, parallel pilots are common. we can run hosted with aggressive caching and a dedicated small pool in your VPC for apples-to-apples. we'll capture cost and quality metrics and recommend final posture.

[00:16:28] [00:16:28] Alex: what about model drift detection during pilot?

[00:16:31] Ethan: Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can set thresholds for ROUGE declines or hallucination rates and alert.

[00:16:45] Samir: ok can you spell out exact artifacts we'll get after the 48-hour run?

[00:16:50] Maya: sure — you'll receive: benchmark spreadsheet (tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, GPU util, cost breakdown), Redwood Console access for the pilot period, perf profile (batching curves, kernel choices), and an executive summary with recommended pilot configuration.

[00:17:12] Dr. Lina: good. on quality, we need to ensure no regression compared to our current model. how will that be measured?

[00:17:18] Ethan: we'll do A/B: sample 500 requests, run current vendor and Redwood variants, compute automated metrics and run 20 human raters for a spot-check. any regression beyond pre-agreed tolerance (we can propose 3% ROUGE drop) flags investigation.

[00:17:40] [00:17:40] Jo: legal/procurement — any contract minimums for Dedicated?

[00:17:44] Maya: Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts usually monthly with minimums depending on GPU type; for pilots we offer short-term commitment options. procurement will receive a pilot SoW.

[00:18:00] Alex: are there any hidden costs we should be aware of?

[00:18:03] Ethan: watch for storage of logs, long-term retention on the Console, and dedicated inter-region egress if you run cross-region fallbacks. we'll list them in the pricing sheet.

[00:18:20] Dr. Lina: quick question about concurrency — when you say batch size 4, is that consistent with 220 qps peak?

[00:18:26] Ethan: batching interacts with concurrency — if you have 220 qps and micro-batch window 20ms you'd accumulate ~4.4 requests per window, so batch 4 is plausible. but spikes vary; autoscaling and burst capacity helps smooth.

[00:18:50] [00:18:50] Maya: OK let's catalog open risks: 1) quality regression risk with quant/4-bit, 2) pilot budget slightly above target if reuse is lower than expected, 3) setup time for Private.

[00:19:05] Samir: i'll own infrastructure and will validate KMS & VPC connectivity.

[00:19:10] Dr. Lina: i'll lead quality validation and provide labeled eval cases.

[00:19:14] Alex: i'll track product acceptance criteria and UI latency tolerance.

[00:19:20] Ethan: to be concrete on the benchmark, we'll simulate traffic with median sequence length 256 and tail length 1024 for the few long notes. we'll run the hosted case first because it's fastest.

[00:19:38] [00:19:38] Maya: we'll follow up with an email packing the artifacts: perf profiles, benchmark plan, sanitized trace schema, pricing sheet draft, and pilot SoW.

[00:19:50] Dr. Lina: sounds good. any further Qs from anyone?

[00:19:54] Jo: just one: if we need compliance documentation fast, who do we contact?

[00:19:58] Maya: i'll loop in security and customer success; we'll attach SOC2 and relevant docs in the follow-up.

[00:20:06] Ethan: quick aside on the math — i'll email a sensitivity table showing cost vs reuse % and quant factor.

[00:20:12] [00:20:12] Alex: excellent.

[00:20:15] Maya: ok we'll move into scheduling — samir, you'll share traces by tomorrow?

[00:20:20] Samir: yes i'll upload a sanitized subset by 2025-06-19.

[00:20:24] Dr. Lina: and we'll provide 500 evaluation examples by 2025-06-19.

[00:20:30] Maya: perfect. recap and explicit next steps: 1) maya send pricing + SoW + perf profiles (due 6/20), 2) ethan run 48hr hosted synthetic benchmark and upload spreadsheet (due 6/25), 3) samir share sanitized traces (due 6/19), 4) joint follow-up meeting week of 6/30.

[00:20:56] [00:20:56] Jo: thanks everyone.
[00:20:58] Alex: thanks.
[00:21:00] Maya: thanks all, we'll share notes and action items.

[00:21:05] -- End of meeting transcript (system generated, transcription imperfect; names sometimes misattributed)

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard words and acronyms (e.g., kernel names, KV cache spelled out), filler words left in for realism.

Benchmark plan (brief):
- Phase 1: Hosted synthetic benchmark (48 hours) simulating 9–11am spike; metrics: qps, p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, cost per effective token.
- Phase 2: Trace replay (sanitized) against two variants (hosted, dedicated) for quality and latency validation.
- Metrics report: CSV + Redwood Console access + executive summary.

Cost model summary (brief):
- Baseline hosted per-output-token: $0.00045–$0.0009 (fp16, varies by model/instance).
- Dedicated + quantization (4-bit) potential: $0.00025–$0.0004 effective per token with cache & batching.
- Example calc: 6M tokens/week * $0.0006 = $3,600/week -> $14.4k/mo baseline. With 25% caching + 1.8x quant + 1.15 batching -> effective multiplier 0.36 -> ~$5.2k/mo.

Pilot timeline summary:
- Week 0 (this week): share pricing, perf profiles, sanitized trace schema.
- Week 1: run 48-hr hosted benchmark (Ethan).
- Week 2: analyze + replay traces; option to provision dedicated nodes.
- Week 3: pilot configuration and decision meeting.
